groups.title: Core Language Concepts
groups.question: You are writing a small Python script that reads a list of orders, filters the paid ones and totals them by customer. Explain the Python features you would use and how you would organise the code.

followUps.Variables, Types, and Control Flow: How does Python's dynamic typing affect how you write and debug code?
followUps.Functions and Module System: What do *args and **kwargs let a function accept?
followUps.List Comprehensions and Dict Patterns: When would you use a list or dict comprehension instead of a loop?

evidence.text: Variables do not declare types; a name can hold any type and the type belongs to the value.
Built-in types like int, str, list and dict cover most data.
Blocks for if, for and while are defined by indentation, not braces.
Functions are values that can be passed around and returned.
*args collects extra positional arguments and **kwargs collects extra keyword arguments.
Code is split into modules and reused with import.

misconceptions.text: Says a list used as a default argument is created fresh on every call.

evidence.text: A comprehension builds a list, set or dict from an iterable in one expression.
It can filter items with an if clause while transforming them.
Comprehensions suit simple transformations; complex logic reads better as a loop.

groups.title: Object-Oriented Python and Error Handling
groups.question: You are modelling customers and premium customers in Python, and reading a file that might be missing. Explain how classes and exceptions help.

followUps.Classes, Objects, and Inheritance: How do __init__ and inheritance work in Python classes?
followUps.Exception Handling with try/except: How would you handle a missing file and define your own error?

evidence.text: __init__ sets up a new object's attributes.
A subclass inherits behaviour from its parent and can override methods.
Special methods like __str__ or __eq__ customise how objects behave with built-in operations.
try and except catch specific errors at runtime.
finally runs cleanup code whether or not an error happened.
Custom exceptions subclass Exception so callers can catch your specific error.

notEnough: Only saying you use try and except.

misconceptions.text: Says catching every exception with a bare except is good practice.

groups.title: Environment and Package Management
groups.question: A teammate cannot run your project because their global Python has different package versions. Explain how you would isolate and reproduce the environment.

followUps.Virtual Environments with venv: What problem does a virtual environment solve?
followUps.Installing Packages with pip: How do pip and requirements.txt make the setup reproducible?

evidence.text: A virtual environment gives the project its own Python packages.
Different projects can use different versions without conflicts.
You activate it before installing packages so they go into the project, not globally.

notEnough: Only saying venv creates an environment.

evidence.text: pip installs packages from the Python Package Index.
pip freeze writes the exact installed versions to a requirements file.
Installing from that file recreates the same environment elsewhere.

groups.title: Python Tooling
groups.question: Your script gives a wrong total and the code style differs across the team. Explain how you would debug it and keep the style consistent.

followUps.Interactive REPL and Debugging: How would you inspect what is happening inside the script while it runs?
followUps.Code Style with PEP 8: What is PEP 8 and how do you enforce it automatically?

evidence.text: The interactive REPL lets you try small pieces of code instantly.
breakpoint() pauses the program so you can inspect variables.
The debugger lets you step through code line by line.

notEnough: Only saying you add print statements.

evidence.text: PEP 8 is Python's official style guide for naming, spacing and line length.
Linters like flake8 report style problems.
Formatters like black rewrite code automatically, so the team stops debating style.

notEnough: Only saying PEP 8 is a style guide.
